statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail steps back into the low band because the overnight Globex tape produced an observed completed retracement off a new session low while the 10-year held flat at 5.117% and WTI eased 0.75%. Stress stays elevated on a 2007-high long end and October hike odds around 57-70%.
recommendation: Tail is below the watch threshold. The published danger window remains the 24 September U.S. cash open, 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, where opening-auction continuation against an aligned rates backdrop is the structure that would deny retracement. The 17:00 UTC seven-year note auction is a secondary long-end checkpoint. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures buy back a new overnight low as the 10-year yield stalls flat at 5.117%
body:
The live Globex path is the decisive evidence and it has improved materially since the previous assessment. Nasdaq-100 December futures trade 30,746.50, down 18.25 points or 0.06%, quoted at 01:15 UTC. The overnight session spans a 108.50-point band between 30,704.50 and 30,813.00, worth 0.35%. The important detail is what happened inside that band: price extended to a new session low at 30,704.50 and was then bought back roughly 42 points. That is an observed, completed retracement, which is the direct opposite of the shallow-pullback and failed-retracement structure that Tail measures. E-mini S&P 500 futures at 7,766.25, down 0.08%, track rather than diverge. The prior cash session was orderly if clearly risk-off: the Nasdaq-100 closed 30,470.29, down 262.10 points or 0.85%, having traded 30,353.88 to 30,706.23 and reclaimed roughly 116 points off its low into the bell.

The rates impulse that drove Wednesday's decline has stalled rather than extended. The 10-year Treasury yield is quoted 5.117% for 24 September, effectively unchanged on the day after Wednesday's roughly 13 to 16 basis point surge to 5.12 to 5.13%, a level last seen in 2007. The 2-year is 4.899%, also flat, so neither the front end nor the long end is currently extending. For reference, the Federal Reserve H.15 constant-maturity series for 22 September stood at 4.71% for the 2-year, 4.96% for the 10-year and 5.29% for the 30-year, which frames the size of Wednesday's move. That move followed September flash PMIs far above consensus, with manufacturing at 57 against about 53.6 to 53.7 expected and services at 58.7, alongside Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr signalling that further policy adjustment is likely needed. Market-implied odds of a 25 basis point hike on 28 October sit between roughly 57.6% on CME futures and about 70% on other readings.

Cross-asset evidence is non-confirming, which is what allows Tail to step down. WTI trades $91.47, down 0.75% from its $92.16 settlement, so the second inflation channel is easing rather than compounding. VIX at 15.18, up 6.83%, remains a low absolute level. Gold at $4,334.40, up 0.37%, shows a modest bid without panic hedging. Most notably, Japan's Nikkei 225 trades 66,156.93, up 1.75%, extending gains rather than cascading risk-off, so Asia is not transmitting the U.S. rates move into a global one-way equity path. Shared Finviz context collected at 23:14 UTC is 131 minutes old and therefore stale under the 90-minute freshness rule, and it is additionally partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable. Its latest-session breadth showed Technology down 0.81%, Communication Services down 1.82%, semiconductors as an industry down 1.67%, three of eight megacaps positive and zero of seven tracked semiconductor names positive. That describes Wednesday's closed cash session, cannot establish current NQ structure, and is superseded here by fresher live evidence.

The forward shape is conditional rather than observed. Risk stays near the horizon floor through the thin Asian stretch, rebuilds at the European cash open as global long-end pricing reaches cash markets, and peaks across the 12:30 UTC jobless-claims block and the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open. The day carries an unusually dense Fed-speaker calendar, with Williams, Barkin, Hammack and Paulson all scheduled, plus a seven-year note auction at 17:00 UTC that is a credible mechanism for a delayed second leg in yields if it is poorly bid. Those are checkpoints, not Tail blocks. Event importance, hawkish repricing and a 5%-plus long end raise Stress and shape Confidence; only an observed price path that denies retracement would raise Tail.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours contain one regime break and a long, steady decay afterwards. Through the 23 September overnight and European morning, Claude published Tail between 10 and 15 with Stress in the low-to-mid 30s while the Nasdaq-100 held a quiet range. The 14:00 UTC hour marked the change: the flash PMI beat, its four-year-high input-cost reading and the surge in the 10-year to a 2007 high pushed Tail to 25 and Stress to 54 in a trend-down assessment, the only orange hour of the window. Tail then decayed to a 20 to 24 watch-band plateau as the cash session retraced into a close roughly 116 points off its low, and the last three published hours all sat at 20 with Stress easing from 52 to 51. Confidence held a narrow 84 to 88 band throughout, reflecting continuously available live futures evidence and verified primary rates and oil data.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are shaped by an unresolved rates backdrop rather than by an observed one-way equity path, and the current hour supplies direct evidence that mean reversion is still working. Conditional risk eases through the thin 02:00 to 06:00 UTC Asian stretch to a modelled floor of Tail 16, then rebuilds at the 07:00 UTC European cash open as global long-end pricing reaches cash markets. Risk crosses into the watch band from 11:00 UTC and peaks at Tail 24 across 13:00 to 14:00 UTC, covering the 12:30 UTC jobless-claims block and the 13:30 UTC cash open, which is why the danger window is drawn at 13:30 to 15:00 UTC. That window reflects the risk of opening-auction continuation denying retracement, not the scheduled data itself. A secondary conditional bump at 17:00 UTC reflects the seven-year note auction as a possible delayed second-leg mechanism for yields. Risk then holds through the power hour and decays after the 20:00 UTC cash close and the 22:00 UTC Globex restart to a horizon minimum of Tail 14. Confidence declines from 88 to 78 across the horizon purely as a function of distance from currently observable evidence.

The 10-year is flat at 5.117% after Wednesday's 2007-high surge and WTI is down 0.75%. Mean reversion is functioning.

Assumption: no overnight headline re-prices the Treasury long end

Conditional trigger: bund and gilt opens extending the US long-end move

forecast.analysis: Final hour before the European cash open. Conditional risk ticks up as liquidity returns and global long-end pricing begins to transmit into index futures. Nothing in this window is observed; the step is a scheduled-liquidity adjustment rather than a structural read.
drivers: Returning European liquidity ahead of the 07:00 UTC cash open
Long-end repricing is the transmission channel to watch, not equity flow
Assumption: the Asian session closes without a directional break

forecast.analysis: European cash open. Conditional risk rebuilds to the current-hour level as European rates and equity markets price Wednesday's US move in cash for the first time. A gap-and-go continuation in index futures here would be the first genuine Tail amplifier of the horizon.
drivers: European cash equity and rates markets open at 07:00 UTC
